ai.title: Checkpoint git ops move to worker thread
ai.summary: CheckpointManager delegates storeFileState and restoreFileState to new checkpoint-worker.ts via worker_threads. Prevents main-thread blocking during git commits and restores. Requires bun run build to generate dist/workers/checkpoint-worker.js before local execution.

eli5.text: The assistant now saves your progress in a separate background worker instead of blocking the main interface during git operations. Previously, when saving checkpoints of your conversation and file state, the entire application would pause until the git commit or restore finished; now those git tasks run on a worker thread, so the interface stays responsive. This only affects the internal checkpointing system used by the agent infrastructure, not something you interact with directly.

ai.title: Fix empty response handling in main-prompt.ts
ai.summary: Replace fallback string 'I'll continue.' with '<end_turn></end_turn>' in assistant message content when fullResponse is empty. This forces the model to end the turn instead of hallucinating continuation text. Affects backend/src/main-prompt.ts message construction logic.

eli5.text: When the assistant generates a reply, there are rare moments it produces nothing at all. Previously, the system filled that gap with the words 'I'll continue.', which made the assistant seem like it was still talking even though it hadn't actually said anything. Now, instead of making something up, the system tells the assistant to cleanly stop and hand the conversation back to you. You won't see a placeholder line anymore when the assistant has genuinely run out of something to say. Only internal users running this version will experience the change today.

ai.title: Fix case for truncating messages
ai.summary: Refactored `getMessagesSubset` in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` to handle the case where no subgoal is marked complete. The logic was simplified by removing an early return and using a ternary operator within the `trimMessagesToFitTokenLimit` call. This ensures consistent message trimming behavior regardless of subgoal status.

eli5.text: When the assistant is working through a task in steps, it sometimes needs to shorten the conversation history to stay within token limits. Previously, if none of those in-progress steps were marked as completed, the trimming logic would behave inconsistently, returning the full message list instead of properly trimming it. This fix makes sure the conversation is always trimmed the same way, regardless of whether any steps are marked complete or not. The behavior is live and applies to internal task handling.

ai.title: Improve error handling in main prompt execution
ai.summary: Refactored `main-prompt.ts` to extract tool result rendering into a new `renderToolResults` utility in `parse-tool-call-xml.ts`. Updated `websocket-action.ts` to catch errors from `mainPrompt`, append `<end_turn>` to error responses, and explicitly reconstruct `messageHistory` with the failed prompt and tool results before sending the response. This ensures the client receives a consistent state and proper termination signal even when backend execution fails.

eli5.text: When something goes wrong while the assistant is handling your request, it now sends you a clear signal that the turn is over (<end_turn>) along with the error message, instead of stopping without telling you it's done. This helps the conversation stay in sync and makes sure you don't get stuck waiting for a reply that will never come.

ai.title: Update menu greeting
ai.summary: Modified welcome message string in npm-app/src/menu.ts displayGreeting. Appended 'today' and pie emoji to prompt. Internal UI text change only.

eli5.text: The main welcome message you see when opening the app now ends with the word 'today' and includes a pie emoji. You'd notice the extra word and friendly icon appear in the same greeting line that already shows your name, if you're signed in. The change only affects this internal text display and is live today.

ai.title: CheckpointManager gates list and detail methods on enabled flag
ai.summary: getLatestCheckpoint and getCheckpointsAsString in npm-app/src/checkpoints/checkpoint-manager.ts now return null or a red 'Checkpoints not enabled: project too large.' string when this.enabled is false. getCheckpointDetails removed entirely. getBareRepoPath visibility narrowed to private.

eli5.text: If you open a project that is too big, the assistant will no longer try to save or show checkpoint snapshots of your files, and instead it will tell you in red text that checkpoints are not enabled for this project. Behind the scenes, the part of the program that listed checkpoints now checks one setting first and stops early when that setting is off, and a separate lookup that gave extra details about one checkpoint has been removed. You won't see checkpoints appear or update on large projects anymore, and a helper that used to find the project's hidden storage folder for these snapshots is now kept private so only that same part of the program can use it.

ai.title: Export fs for checkpoint tests
ai.summary: Added `export { fs }` in `npm-app/src/checkpoints/file-manager.ts` to support testing. This change aligns with fixing checkpoint tests. Scope limited to checkpoint file manager and related test files.

eli5.text: The assistant's developers made a behind-the-scenes tweak to a testing file so they can verify the assistant saves and restores its progress correctly. This only affects their internal testing process, not your experience. You won't notice any difference when using the assistant today. It's just housekeeping to make sure future improvements are stable.

ai.title: Fix credits calculation and referral link generation
ai.summary: Removed referral link generation from backend usage responses and fixed frontend credits calculation by introducing a `pendingRequestId` guard to prevent race conditions during concurrent requests. Referral links in CLI now use static environment variables instead of dynamic backend payloads. Updated `npm-app` build script to copy worker files to `dist`.

eli5.text: You may have noticed your referral link disappeared from the authentication success message and your usage panel, and it now pulls from a fixed system setting rather than a dynamic backend payload. The client also stops double-counting credits when you fire multiple requests at once by ignoring usage updates tied to an in-flight request, which fixes the credits calculation bug where your displayed balance could jump incorrectly. Additionally, the app install package now includes a set of background worker files that were previously missing from the built output, which the CLI could not load before. All changes are tied to this snapshot; no rollout date beyond today is indicated.

ai.title: Remove workers copy from npm-app postbuild
ai.summary: postbuild script in npm-app/package.json no longer copies src/workers to dist/src/workers. Change reverts prior addition of worker bundling step. Scope limited to npm-app build pipeline. tsc-alias remains final step.

eli5.text: The build process for the application no longer copies worker files into the final package during the build step. This affects the internal build pipeline, and if you looked at the build steps, you'd notice the command that used to copy these worker files is now gone, simplifying the post-build process.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.177
ai.summary: Version bump to 1.0.177. Updates `npm-app/package.json`. Internal change.

eli5.text: You can now install version 1.0.177 of the AI assistant software, which bundles several smaller improvements made over the past day. These improvements include clearer error messages when the chat response is cut off, better tracking of your usage credits, a friendlier welcome message in the menu, and the ability to use new example prompts for coding tasks. The update also moves some internal work into the background to keep the app feeling smooth while it processes. Updating to this version keeps your install current with all the latest fixes and features.

ai.title: Fix checkpoint manager import path
ai.summary: Corrected relative import path in `npm-app/src/checkpoints/checkpoint-manager.ts`. Replaced `src/project-files` with `../project-files` to ensure proper module resolution. Minor whitespace formatting adjustments also included.

eli5.text: The program that saves and restores your work sessions now correctly finds the file that defines the project boundary. You wouldn't see anything new yourself, but behind the scenes the loading of each session will no longer break when it tries to locate your project root. This is pure housekeeping: the fix is already in place and affects anyone running the version that includes it.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.178
ai.summary: Version bumped from 1.0.177 to 1.0.178 in `npm-app/package.json`. No functional changes, bug fixes, or feature additions are present in this commit. This is a routine release increment for the `codebuff` package.

eli5.text: The assistant's release was renumbered to a new version, which bundles recent behind-the-scenes fixes. The most visible repair corrects how saved checkpoints are located, so the assistant will load prior conversation states correctly instead of stumbling on a missing file. This update is live today as part of the new release. If you use the assistant, the checkpoint fix happens automatically and you shouldn't encounter the loading glitch anymore.

ai.title: Print prompt during evals
ai.summary: Added console log in evals/scaffolding.ts loopMainPrompt to print the prompt before execution. Uses picocolors blue for visibility. Internal evals tooling change.

eli5.text: When the system runs automated tests on how the assistant responds, it now prints out the prompt it's testing before it starts, shown in blue text so it's easy to spot. This is purely a behind-the-scenes change for the internal tools engineers use to check the assistant's behavior.

ai.title: Clarify tool visibility in prompts
ai.summary: Updated tool descriptions in `backend/src/tools.ts` to explicitly state that Buffy sees tool definitions while the user does not. Changed headers from `##` to `###` for consistency and replaced concrete file paths with placeholders in usage examples. Rewrote `toolsInstructions` to define the assistant-user interaction model and clarify parsing expectations.

eli5.text: The assistant now gets clearer instructions about which tools it can see and use versus which ones only the user sees, so it knows the boundaries of its own capabilities. The internal tool descriptions were rewritten to spell out how the assistant and user interact, and formatting was tidied up for consistency. You wouldn't notice this directly, but the assistant will give cleaner, more accurate responses because its own guidance is less ambiguous.

ai.title: Add colored diff output to SWE-bench eval
ai.summary: Added console logging of the generated git patch in `evals/swe-bench-eval.ts`. Uses `picocolors` to highlight additions in green, deletions in red, and hunk headers in cyan. This change is internal to the evaluation harness and does not affect the Freebuff CLI or Web UI.

eli5.text: When the system runs an internal test to check if a coding problem was solved correctly, it now prints the step-by-step changes it found in color on the screen. Lines showing new code appear in green, removed code in red, and section markers in cyan, so someone watching the test can quickly see what changed. Only people working directly on the testing tools will see this new colored output; it won't show up in the Freebuff app or website.
